source.title: Depth-Dependent Safety Geometry in Vision-Language Models: Layer-Wise Localization and Bidirectional Refusal Control
source.authors: M. Karamat; Syed Talal Hassan; Christian García

record.tranche_reason: Tests refusal behavior under representation-level interventions, using activation scaling and steering rather than the fine-tuning or response-token measurements in the claim.
record.gate_note: The study does not test fine-tuning, benign training data, per-token KL, compliant-opening prefills, suffixes, decoding changes, weight/rank localization, or training to deepen safety. It does report refusal rates under activation scaling and steering, and layer-wise angular-divergence patterns. Its white-box interventions are not evidence that an external input can realize the same shifts.
record.test_reason: The study does not test any version. It applies inference-time activation scaling and mean-difference steering to visual-token activations in frozen VLMs (Qwen3-VL-4B; InternVL2.5-4B for geometry only). It reports refusal rates, but there is no fine-tuning (V1, V2), no per-token KL over response positions (V3), and no prefill, suffix or decoding attack (V4). The interventions edit activations, not a small set of weights or ranks (V5). It has no causal account of shallowness (V6) and no deepening training (V7). Qi et al. is cited only in related work. Its refusal-rate findings are a related construct and are recorded under fits_no_version. The reader's 'tests/T2' is incorrect.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors also stress that representational separability does not imply causal controllability, since layer 20 separates safe from unsafe but steering it barely changes behaviour. They frame the work as exposing a white-box attack surface, and note no input-level attack is shown.
record.recipe_differences: Inference-time activation scaling and directional steering in frozen vision-language models; not fine-tuning, response-position KL measurement, or token-opening interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: Behavioral outcomes vary with activation magnitude, layer region, steering strength, and steering scope (focused versus global). Divergence patterns and layer locations differ between Qwen3-VL-4B and InternVL2.5-4B; causal interventions were run only on Qwen3-VL-4B.

fits_no_version.finding: In Qwen3-VL-4B, global mean-difference steering on vision layers 7–10 moves unsafe rejection from 84% to 6% (alpha=4) or 96% (alpha=-4). Focused (CLS+10 tokens) and later-layer (18–20) steering leave URR near 80–84%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal in VLMs can be bidirectionally controlled by activation steering in early vision-encoder layers, with effect dependent on layer and token scope.

fits_no_version.finding: Uniform activation magnitude scaling changes URR and SRR together. Examples: vision 7–10 at alpha 0.85 gives URR 100 and SRR 99/100; vision 18–22 at 1.15 gives URR 96 and SRR 91; language at 0.85 lowers URR to 37.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Activation magnitude scaling shifts overall refusal propensity in VLMs with a safety–selectivity trade-off rather than selective safety.

fits_no_version.finding: Safe–unsafe angular divergence is depth-dependent in both models: strongest in early language layers, heterogeneous in vision encoders.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: VLMs show depth-dependent safe–unsafe representational geometry, and separability does not imply steerability.

record.peer_reviewed: 40th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2026), Workshop: Foundations of Language Model Security
record.problems: Causal interventions are only on Qwen3-VL-4B and require white-box access to internal activations; no external input-level attack is demonstrated. InternVL2.5-4B receives representational analysis only, described qualitatively. The authors note that broader held-out evaluation is needed; the reported MMLU check uses 100 samples.
record.rows_left_out: To stay within 60 rows, omitted the alpha=0.90 Unsafe-bench values for all three Table 1 regions, most Table 2 Google Conceptual Captions conditions and regions, and other Safe Rejection Rate values in Tables 1–3. Kept the stated baseline, salient endpoints, and rows that illustrate reported layer/scope effects and selectivity changes.

untested.parts: No aligned-vs-base per-token KL across response positions; the layer-wise angular divergence is over network depth, not token positions.
No prefilling, suffix or decoding attacks. The white-box activation steering is explicitly not an input-level attack.
No weight or rank localization. Layer regions and token scopes of activation interventions are not parameter localization.
No test of data or objective causes.

record.verdict_notes: The record's relation (tests) and tranche (T2) are overridden. The reader's own per-version statuses were all not_tested, so relation is cites_only/T6. The study cites Qi et al. only in related work. The omitted alpha=0.90 and GCC rows are declared in rows_left_out and bear on no version.

versions.untested_parts: No harmful-example fine-tuning or post-fine-tuning compliance measurement.
No benign-data fine-tuning or resulting harmful-compliance measurement.
No aligned-versus-base per-token KL measurement across response positions.
No compliant-opening prefills, adversarial suffixes, or decoding changes; the interventions operate on internal activations.
No weight or rank localization or editing. The study compares activation steering scopes over visual tokens, not a small set of parameters.
No test of whether data or a training objective causes shallow safety.
No training to deepen safety or evaluation of whether such training holds up.
